title: Air India Mumbai-Toronto Flights Start October 25, Westbound via Rome
excerpt: The seasonal three-times-weekly service runs through March 26, 2027 on a 328-seat Boeing 777-300ER. Air India announced it as nonstop, but its latest schedule shows the westbound flight stopping in Rome for a total journey of more than 20 hours, with the return nonstop.
body:
• Air India starts seasonal Mumbai-Toronto flights on Sunday, October 25, running three times a week on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays through March 26, 2027.
  • The airline's latest schedule, reported by Simple Flying on October 21, shows the westbound flight stopping at Rome Fiumicino, taking more than 20 hours in total, while the Toronto-Mumbai return operates nonstop.
  • Flights use a 328-seat Boeing 777-300ER with 8 first-class suites, 40 lie-flat business seats and 280 economy seats, adding nearly 2,000 seats a week between India and Canada.
  • Reader check before booking: the two directions are not the same journey — westbound AI193 leaves Mumbai at 12:25 am and reaches Toronto at 11:00 am via Rome, while eastbound AI192 leaves Toronto at 1:30 pm and arrives in Mumbai at 2:10 pm the next day.

Air India will launch its seasonal Mumbai-Toronto service in four days, on October 25, filling the gap left when Air Canada withdrew from the Toronto-Mumbai market earlier this year, according to Simple Flying. The change in the airline's latest schedule is the detail travellers need to see first: a service announced as nonstop will, westbound, stop in Rome.

In its official announcement, Air India said it would launch a seasonal three-times-weekly non-stop service between Mumbai and Toronto between October 25, 2026 and March 26, 2027, making it the only carrier operating direct flights between the two cities and adding nearly 2,000 seats each week.

"Canada is one of Air India's most important international markets, with deep people-to-people connections driving strong demand for travel, particularly during the festive and holiday season."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

Westbound via Rome, Eastbound Nonstop

Until recently the service was listed as nonstop in both directions. Simple Flying reported on October 21 that the latest schedule instead shows the westbound flight stopping at Rome Fiumicino Airport, with total block time of more than 20 hours including the layover, while the return from Toronto to Mumbai operates nonstop.

The published timings are asymmetric. Westbound AI193 leaves Mumbai at 12:25 am, reaches Rome at 5:30 am, departs Rome at 7:00 am and arrives in Toronto at 11:00 am, on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. Eastbound AI192 leaves Toronto at 1:30 pm and arrives in Mumbai at 2:10 pm the following day. Simple Flying linked the Rome stop to Air India's avoidance of Russian, Iranian and Pakistani airspace, noting that its existing Mumbai flights to New York JFK and Newark also stop at Fiumicino to refuel and change crew, with westbound headwinds as another factor.

The Aircraft and the Market

The route uses a 328-seat Boeing 777-300ER with upgraded interiors: eight first-class suites with privacy doors in a 1-2-1 layout, 40 lie-flat business-class seats in a 1-2-1 layout, and 280 economy seats arranged mainly in 3-4-3 with 31 inches of pitch, with Wi-Fi on board, according to both Air India and Simple Flying.

The market is large. Booking data cited by Simple Flying put Mumbai-Toronto at more than 1.2 million round-trip passengers between June 2025 and May 2026 in the wider India-Toronto market, with Toronto the third-largest Mumbai-North America market behind New York JFK and San Francisco in its reporting. Air Canada had operated the route four times a week via London Heathrow on a fifth-freedom basis until March this year, after earlier nonstop operations from 2017 to 2020 became unviable without Russian airspace.

Canada Network This Winter

Through its Mumbai and Delhi hubs, Air India said Toronto passengers can connect to Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kochi, Ludhiana and Vadodara, among other Indian cities. For the winter 2026-27 season the airline will operate 20 flights a week between India and Canada: 10 a week from Delhi to Toronto, three a week from Mumbai to Toronto and seven a week from Delhi to Vancouver. Overall capacity between India and Canada rises by about 4,400 seats a month, with premium seat capacity to Toronto up 71 per cent, the airline said.

Air India said flights are available for booking across its website and mobile app, its customer contact centre and travel agents worldwide. For diaspora travellers in the Greater Toronto Area heading to Mumbai for the festive and holiday season, the practical point is to price the two directions separately: the westbound journey is a 20-hour-plus trip with a Rome stop, while the return is nonstop, and that difference affects connections, sleep and arrival-day plans.
